look_here_first: ANATHERUM TENUISPATHEUM is an accepted distinct bluestem, old Andropogon glomeratus var. pumilus 'ROBUST VARIANT', NOT the separate accepted Southwestern Anatherum eremicum (= var. scabriglumis). A published Texas-authored key supports typically SMOOTH sheaths, enclosing raceme sheath <2.5 mm, true ligule membrane <1 mm with LONG cilia, sessile spikelet <3.8 mm. Contrast eremicum's scabrous sheaths, >2.5 mm raceme sheath, 1–2 mm membrane with short cilia, >4.2 mm spikelets. The current archived source-labelled flowering photograph lacks a ruler, true ligule and spikelet macro: no ID hold clearance. Compare A. glomeratum and virginicum separately.

field_id_lesson.look_here_first: ANATHERUM TENUISPATHEUM: a third, separately accepted bluestem species. Kew treats old Andropogon glomeratus var. pumilus (and A. tenuispatheus) as synonyms here, NOT under A. glomeratum. Compare a whole mature flowering culm, spathe enclosing each paired raceme, then a mm-scale sessile/pedicellate spikelet pair against true A. glomeratum and A. virginicum; the existing photo alone is insufficient to separate these.
crew_checkpoints: Document the entire flowering culm and where each raceme pair emerges from its spathe.
Measure the spathe and raceme length from a mature specimen; retain actual measurements rather than guessing species-level thresholds.
At 10–20× magnification photograph the rachis joints, paired spikelets, awn insertion and visible hairs with a millimeter reference.
Photograph the leaf collar and ligule, then compare the complete reproductive unit against source-verified specimens.
For tenuispatheum, check generally smooth sheaths, raceme sheaths usually under 2.5 mm wide, a ligule membrane under 1 mm with long marginal hairs, and sessile spikelets usually under 3.8 mm.
The eremicus contrast has rough sheaths, usually wider raceme sheaths, a 1–2 mm membrane with shorter hairs, and sessile spikelets usually over 4.2 mm. Use the combined characters.

IMPORTANT missing fourth accepted genus look-alike A. eremicum: smooth/<2.5 mm raceme sheath/<1 mm long-ciliate ligule/<3.8 mm sessile spikelet supports tenuispatheum versus often scabrous/>2.5 mm sheath/1–2 mm short-ciliate ligule/>4.2 mm spikelet in eremicum (Wipff & Shaw 2018). Do not auto-add fourth canonical card.

look_alikes.check: Bushy bluestem has a conspicuously dense brushlike crown of many crowded silky short racemes; do not equate one fluffy pair with the whole crown.
Broomsedge typically shows more individually separated spathe-enclosed flowering units; confirm by spathe and spikelet detail.
Little bluestem produces silky racemes on separate branches; compare branch placement and spikelet structure.

For tenuispatheum, check generally smooth sheaths, raceme sheaths usually under 2.5 mm wide, a ligule membrane under 1 mm with long marginal hairs, and sessile spikelets usually under 3.8 mm. The eremicus contrast has rough sheaths, usually wider raceme sheaths, a 1–2 mm membrane with shorter hairs, and sessile spikelets usually over 4.2 mm. Use the combined characters.
